analysis.title: GS Blekos - Marketcolour + Coreweave / Infineon / Siemens Energy / Zalando / FLS / ABN 11 Nov 2026
key_insights: US equities closed lower on 11/10 after a hot CPI print of +30bps vs consensus +20bps, the third consecutive month with a 0.1% beat. SPX -38bps to 7520, NDX -60bps to 27740, RTY -68bps to 2821. The 2Y UST had its worst day since Oct 2024.
Sector breadth was mixed: 5 of 11 S&P sectors finished higher, Financials +0.49% and Tech -1.40%. NDX weakness was concentrated in Semis, Memory and Neoclouds.
GS floor activity was a 5 on a 1-10 scale. Asset managers were moderate net sellers on supply in large cap tech. Hedge funds were net sellers (short > long), concentrated in tech and macro products.

GS expects a second 25bp Fed hike in December and adds a third 25bp hike to its forecast for March 2027. A January hike is possible, but March is more likely because GS expects softer November and December inflation reports followed by larger start-of-year price increases in January.

CoreWeave (+8% post market, GS would add to positions): implied 4Q revenue guidance is 3% above the Street, margins 100bps above, capex 22% below. The company said it will issue no additional parent-level unsecured debt through 2027. Other financing levers are customer prepayments, OEM financing and growing operating cash flow.

CoreWeave contract economics: 4-5 year contracts now price at $20-25mn/MW versus WholeCo revenue/MW of about $10mn and capex of about $40mn/MW. GS now estimates unlevered IRR of 20-30% before residual value, versus 15-21% prior.

Infineon (BUY, PT EUR91, 85% upside): GS raises FY27-30 revenue estimates by c.2-3% on AI power semis demand in the PS segment and improving ATV demand. GM estimates rise 0-1pp, adj. EBIT estimates rise 3-4% and EPS estimates rise 3-4%.

Zalando (BUY, PT EUR44, 60% upside): after hosting the CFO, GS reports 4Q started well with autumn/winter trading on track. The three apps have limited B2C overlap (10%). Management remains confident on the 3-4% retail media target by 2028, sees AI and agentic commerce as growth and efficiency drivers, reports B2B momentum with a full Scayle pipeline, and reiterated the 6-8% 2028 adj. EBIT margin target.

Siemens Energy (CL BUY, PT EUR212, 70% upside): the announced buyback plus dividends implies EUR27bn of value returns out to FY2030, versus Visible Alpha at EUR24bn and GSe at EUR30bn. GS expects the Capital Markets Day to show a stronger profit outlook and a material acceleration in cash flow. Capital allocation to FY2028 is currently 1/3 capex, 1/3 returns and 1/3 retained, and GS expects this to change once FY2030 guidance is added.

FLS 3Q beat: organic orders +32% vs consensus +26%, organic revenue +6% vs consensus +4.6%, EBITA 8% above consensus with margins 100bps ahead. Guidance narrowed to growth +1-3% (prev 0 to 4%) and margin ~16.5% (prev 16-16.5%, consensus 16.6%).

ABN AMRO 3Q net profit beat on higher NII, other income (one-off NIBC gains) and lower loan loss provisions. Revenues were 4% above consensus (NII +2%, fees -2%, other income +82%). Excluding the one-off, revenues were 1% better and pre-provision profit beat by 2%, with costs in line. Provisions showed a release from model updates. Deposits fell QoQ excluding NIBC on seasonal spending and migration into securities.

ITV missed and guided below as digital ad revenue slowed. 3Q26 revenue missed consensus by 1%, with a 2% shortfall in Media & Entertainment (the business being sold). Studios matched consensus but missed GS estimates by 3%. TV advertising revenue fell 8% against guidance of about 5%, and digital advertising growth slowed to 6% over nine months from 13% in 1H.

INWIT 3Q26 results were in line and 2026 guidance was reiterated. A modest positive came from several Italian authorities looking to accelerate resolution of the contract disputes with Swisscom and Telecom Italia.
